name: Siren
description: A plug-in siren with a siren and a chime. Insteon sensors and controllers trigger it when it's armed, and keypads and remotes arm and disarm it, in home mode, away mode or both.

verification.note: The Siren Module Developer Notes give 0x03 as its Get Insteon Engine Version reply in their text and 0x02 in their table and example.
The Siren Module Developer Notes' introduction swaps home and away for groups 1 to 4; their group table, used here, doesn't.

steps.text: Plug the Siren into an unswitched wall outlet.

notes: The Siren is loud; leave the protective film over the speaker to lower the volume, and use hearing protection when testing up close.

steps.text: Press and hold the SET button.

notes: The first device put into linking mode becomes the controller and the second the responder. Linking mode ends after a link is made or after four minutes without one.

To be triggered by a device: put that device in linking mode, tap the Siren's SET button until you hear the alert tone you want (siren or chime), then press and hold the SET button until it double-beeps.

To be armed and disarmed by a device: tap the chosen button on that device and put it in linking mode, tap the Siren's SET button until its status LED glows red, then press and hold the SET button until it double-beeps. Arming takes 45 seconds, during which the Siren beeps.

To add the Siren to a Hub, press and hold its SET button when the app prompts. The Siren 2868-222 Owner's Manual says to hold it until the Siren double-beeps; the Siren 2868-222 Quick Start Guide says until it beeps. Don't use local programming if a Hub or other central controller manages the Siren.

verification.note: Read from the Siren 2868-222 Owner's Manual's local programming flow chart (press and hold the SET button to move to Linking Mode) and its legend (status LED blinks green). Its written steps give the Siren's SET button only for the Siren's side as a responder or when adding it to a Hub, where it is held until the Siren double-beeps.

steps.text: Have the Hub start ALL-Linking as the controller, for group 0.
Press and hold the SET button.
Wait for the Hub to report the new link.
steps.expect: The Hub reports ALL-Linking Completed with the device's Insteon ID

steps.text: Have the Hub send ID Request; the device answers with its category, subcategory and firmware version.

Have the Hub send Enter Linking Mode (cmd1 0x09) with cmd2 0x01, for group 1: as an extended message if Get Insteon Engine Version (cmd1 0x0D) says the device is i2CS, and as a standard message otherwise.
Have the Hub start ALL-Linking as the responder.
steps.expect: The Hub reports ALL-Linking Completed with the device's Insteon ID

steps.text: Have the Hub send Ping a few times to check the link.

notes: This links the Hub's group 0 to the device as a responder, and the device's group 1 to the Hub as a controller.

To add the device without its SET button, have the Hub send it Enter Linking Mode (cmd1 0x09, cmd2 0x01; extended for an i2CS device) right after it starts ALL-Linking, in place of the SET button step.
Once linked, the Hub reads the device's settings with Get Operating Flags and an extended Get for group 1.

verification.note: No document describes this; it's how the device is set up in practice.

steps.text: Press and hold the SET button to enter linking mode.
Tap the SET button to enter multi-linking mode.

notes: Multi-linking mode lasts four minutes, restarting after each link, or until the SET button is tapped.

verification.note: Read from the Siren 2868-222 Owner's Manual's local programming flow chart; the LED pattern is from its legend.

steps.text: Press and hold the SET button to enter linking mode.
Press and hold the SET button again to enter unlinking mode.

notes: Unlinking mode ends after a link is removed or after four minutes.

verification.note: Read from the Siren 2868-222 Owner's Manual's local programming flow chart; the LED pattern is from its legend.

steps.text: Unplug the Siren from its outlet.
Press and hold the SET button while plugging the Siren back in.
Keep holding the SET button until the Siren stops beeping.
steps.expect: Double beep when the reset is complete

notes: Erases all links and customized properties.

steps.text: Remove the device from every scene, as a controller and as a responder.

verification.note: No document describes this; it's how the device is set up in practice.

steps.text: Remove the device from every scene on the Hub first.
Have the Hub send Enter Unlinking Mode (cmd1 0x0A) with cmd2 0x01, for group 1.
Have the Hub start ALL-Linking as the responder, for group 0; the device deletes its group 1 link to the Hub.
Have the Hub start unlinking for group 0 (Start ALL-Linking with link code 0xFF).
Have the Hub send Enter Linking Mode (cmd1 0x09), as an extended message if the device is i2CS.
Wait for the Hub to report that the link is gone.
steps.expect: The Hub reports the device's Insteon ID

notes: The Hub won't remove a device that still belongs to a scene.

verification.note: No document describes this; it's how the device is set up in practice.

notes: As a controller, group 1 is the alert: it broadcasts while the siren sounds.
The Siren Module Developer Notes document firmware 0xE1; their title gives 0xE2.
The LED is green when the siren is armed and red when it's disarmed.
The Siren 2868-222 Owner's Manual gives the siren as 115 dB and the chime as 100 dB at 1 meter; the Siren Module Developer Notes give the siren as 91 dB at 10 cm in one place and 120 dB in another.
The Siren 2868-222 Owner's Manual says it holds 24 links; the Siren Module Developer Notes' memory map allows 416.
The Siren 2868-222 Owner's Manual has the siren tone sound for 2 minutes unless the siren is disarmed, and the chime give two short beeps.
The Siren Module Developer Notes' example broadcasts carry another product's category and subcategory.
